input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds only Customer (not mutual), reaches every Vendor employee rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, runs 24 months, expressly prohibits hiring and employing (a no-hire), and negates any general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out through "regardless of how the employee applies". That fails every fallback element and lands in walk-away territory, and it also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment" and is free to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment". The shortest cure at the preferred position is to replace the covenant with a confirmation that Customer is under no non-solicitation restriction, which also removes the internal conflict with 12.3. A mutual, 12-month, involvement-limited non-solicit with carve-outs remains available as a fallback.

ops.oldText: shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: is not subject to any non-solicitation, no-hire, or similar restriction with respect to Vendor personnel.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the one-sided 24-month solicit/hire bar on Customer, which is walk-away territory for us and contradicts Section 12.3's confirmation that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. If Vendor needs protection, we could accept a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no hiring bar.
proposal.summary: Replace the Customer-only non-solicit/no-hire covenant with a confirmation that Customer is under no such restriction.
